newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to cut H1 coffee exports by 150,000 bags.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to cut H1 coffee exports by 150,000 bags.

text.p: Indonesia will reduce its coffee exports by 150,000 60-kg bags in the first half of this year under a plan adopted by key producers in Brazil, vice-chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, Mustafa Sulaiman, told Reuters on Monday.
He also said a meeting of robusta producers on the resort island of Bali on Thursday had yet to be confirmed.
"We have decided to reduce our exports of robusta by 150,000 bags. The remaining 850,000 bags will have to be allocated among African and other robusta producers," he said.
"Our decision is final. It is not open to negotiations," he said in Nusa Dua, where the International Coffee Organization (ICO) is holding a three-day meeting which opened on Monday.
He said the Indonesian decision was made known at the ACPC meeting in Brazil on January 23.
"We hope robusta producers such as Vietnam will share the allocation (of export cuts) along with the Ivory Coast, Uganda, Brazil, Ecuador and others," he said.
He said the robusta group meeting on Thursday had yet to be confirmed, adding that it was up to the Africans, who spearheaded the drive for export cuts, to initiate the meeting.

"It is still not confirmed. If they come to us and say we want to discuss robusta and please prepare a place, as host we will," said Mustafa, who is head of the organising committee for the ICO meeting and a gathering of producers from the Asia-Pacific area.
"It is up to their (African) initiative," he said. "Uganda is not present at the (ICO) meeting. Uganda is one of the largest producers of robusta in Africa."
He said Uganda had not informed him that its representatives would be present at the Bali meetings.

"We have already taken our share (of cuts). Now it's up to them," he said, adding that Vietnam had also not turned up for the ICO meeting and was not expected to participate in the meeting of Asia-Pacific coffee producers on Thursday.
The ACPC decided last month to reduce members' exports by 1.3 million bags, with one million bags coming from robusta producers and the rest from arabica producers.
African countries had pushed for the cuts in a bid to lift robusta prices.
